targetName: Space Shuttle launch stack (Discovery on pad)

objectClass.primaryType: multi-body crewed launch vehicle stack (winged orbiter + propellant tank + two solid boosters)
motionPotential: separable stage bodies (boosters and tank detach from orbiter)
hinged payload bay doors on the orbiter
materialFamilies: sprayed insulation foam (matte dielectric, saturated orange)
heat-treated metal (metallic, mid roughness) at nozzles
objectClass.notes: Read by direct inspection of the reference; see _shuttle/analysis/image-analysis.md. Not a character or hybrid, so no anatomy track applies.

reasoning: Four macro bodies, not one: tank, two boosters, orbiter. A single-root spec would be shallow by construction.
Occlusion risk is the dominant score. One night view shows one side. The far side of the stack, the orbiter ventral surface and the payload bay interior are never observed.
Silhouette is complex but every sub-form is a primitive: ogive, cylinder, cone, extruded delta, lofted fuselage. No organic or implicit surface is required.
Repetition is real but low-count: booster case joint rings, the cabin window group, elevon split lines.
Action readiness is required by the host page, which explodes the stack and makes each component clickable.
Tier is complex rather than ultra-complex: a 400 x 492 reference cannot support an ultra-complex micro-detail bar.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation: Far side of the entire stack is unobserved. Reconstructed from bilateral symmetry of the assembly and rotational symmetry of tank and boosters. Declared inference.
Orbiter ventral thermal protection faces the tank and is never visible. Reconstructed from published layout.
Payload bay interior is closed in the reference. Modelled as a plain bay and declared inference.
Cabin window count and shape are below the resolution floor; the crew module spans about 20 px. Taken from published layout.
Marking glyph forms are unreadable at this resolution. Placement is observed, letterforms are approximated.
True albedo is unknown because the scene is lit by directional sodium floodlight. De-lighting is required before any colour is transferred to a material.
Aft orbiter-to-tank attach structure is occluded by the orbiter body in this view.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Nose-to-barrel transition ring where the ogive meets the cylindrical barrel.
Vertical conduit line running the full length of the tank, offset from the centreline; reads as a raised narrow ridge casting its own shadow.
Waisted band of different surface treatment between the two tank barrels, at a slightly smaller radius.
Raised circumferential joint rings dividing each booster into case segments. A repetition system, not one-off geometry.
Booster nose is two cone angles: a steeper cap over a shallower frustum, with a step between them.
Aft skirt flares to a larger diameter than the case barrel.
Near-black nose cap distinct from the white fuselage, with a hard boundary.
Cluster of bright window rectangles on the crew module, arranged in two bands.
Dark swept band along each wing leading edge, forming a shallow V outward from the fuselage.
Split line across each wing trailing edge separating inboard from outboard elevon.
Wing planform is double-delta: a shallow-sweep glove ahead of a steeper-sweep outer panel, with a visible break.
USA plus flag on one wing upper surface, NASA plus Discovery on the other. Placement observed, glyphs below resolution.
Two raised pods flanking the fin base at the aft end of the fuselage.
Three bell nozzles clustered at the aft end, one high and two low.
Forward strut standing the orbiter nose off the tank, leaving a visible gap between the two bodies.

anatomy.note: primaryDomain is object, so no anatomy track applies.

definitionOfDone: Silhouette, body proportions and inter-body placement match the reference within perspective error.
All four macro bodies are separate, named, clickable and explodable, and carry the host page group names.
Each of the fifteen detail-inventory entries is realised as geometry or a material override, never prose alone.
Material response separates matte foam, matte tile, matte paint and metallic nozzle, with no albedo reuse across channels.
The model holds up from at least four viewpoints, including the two the reference never shows.
Every unobserved region is reported as inference rather than presented as measured.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: surface looks like flat plastic
local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

featureGroups.name: Inter-body proportions and placement
qualityCriteria: Tank diameter, booster diameter, orbiter span and body lengths hold the measured ratios.
Booster nose apexes sit below the tank nose apex.
Wing tips extend beyond the outer envelope of the boosters.
failureModes: boosters modelled as tall as the tank
wing span shrunk inside the booster envelope
orbiter mounted on the tank centreline instead of standing off on one side

featureGroups.name: Orbiter identity features
qualityCriteria: Double-delta planform with a visible sweep break.
Dark nose cap and dark wing leading-edge band with hard boundaries.
Fin, both pods and three nozzles present at the aft end.
failureModes: single-sweep delta wing
leading edge left white
engine cluster reduced to one nozzle

featureGroups.name: Honest reporting of unobserved regions
qualityCriteria: Every region the single view cannot show is labelled inference in the spec and in the summary.
failureModes: far side presented as measured
payload bay interior claimed from the photo

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
booster-to-tank contact and radial placement delta
dark-region boundary placement delta at nose cap, leading edges and engine bay
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
